answer: Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the vault of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Each submission hangs on the copper of a task receipt, and the inlet is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on escrowed payment for graded work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool.
